newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK people find China migrants rude, greedy - poll.
newsitem.headline: HK people find China migrants rude, greedy - poll.

text.p: A majority of Hong Kong people consider immigrants from mainland China ignorant, rude, dirty and greedy, according to opinion poll results made available on Monday.
The poll, by the Hong Kong Psychological Society, found 51 percent of the people who were quizzed harboured unflattering views of the new immigrants.
Only 27 percent considered mainland immigrants to be hardworking, thrifty and tenacious, according to the poll of 423 Hong Kong-born people, conducted between February 24 and 27.

Up to 54 percent thought their new neighbours brought more ill than good to the territory. Cheap labour was most often cited as the only positive consequence of their arrival, the survey, which was made available to Reuters, showed.
A researcher and lecturer on psychology with the University of Hong Kong told a newspaper the results were alarming.

"It is very clear that many Hong Kong-born people do not like people from the mainland. They view themselves as different from the mainlanders," Chiu Chi-yue told the South China Morning Post. "They believe people from China are inferior," Chiu said.

The vast majority of Hong Kong's 6.4 million people are ethnic Chinese. Many of them, or their parents, themselves fled to Hong Kong ago in search of a better life or as an escape from Communist rule on the mainland. They will be Chinese subjects again, from midnight this June 30, when British rule ends.
The survey findings drew invited a barrage of criticism from local media. "Discrimination against new immigrants, we can't have such attitudes," editorialised the daily Sing Pao.
"With the resumption of Chinese sovereignty in 1997, Hong Kong will become part of China...it is ridiculous for Hong Kong people to discriminate against the new immigrants."
The mass-selling Apple Daily said in its editorial such attitudes would affect Hong Kong's development.
